summary: Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, initially called the brief "bounded" but escalated to ARCHITECTURAL after one clarifying answer, ran a full question/approach flow, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code written, and began writing-plans only after approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria are satisfied based on the session log, on-disk spec file, git status, and screen text. The only wrinkle is a transient initial 'bounded' statement that the agent itself reversed before doing anything, and a stubbed Codex gate that returned incomplete results.

observations.description: Codex spec gate reported broken/stub behavior: 'both lenses (completeness-and-consistency, feasibility-and-scope) returned empty payloads; verdict-normalize scored each incomplete — json payload has no terminal verdict'; 'Runtime: codex-plugin-cc 0.0.0-stub; model and reasoning effort unavailable — there's no config.toml under $CODEX_HOME'. The agent handled it gracefully but the gate produced no review.

The agent's very first output classified the task as 'bounded ... I'll settle the design in chat rather than write a spec' before asking any questions; escalation to architectural only happened after my clarifying answer. A reader skimming could be misled by the initial verdict.
Multi-select tooling question required navigating past 4 options to a separate 'Submit' row, then a second 'Submit answers' confirmation screen — easy to think the answer was already sent.
Spinner label read 'Shenaniganing…' during a long thinking phase — cute, but uninformative about what is actually happening.

The agent added a .gitignore excluding docs/superpowers and docs/hyperpowers, meaning the spec it just wrote is deliberately untracked. Worth confirming that is intended, since criterion language speaks of a 'committed spec file'.

criteria.evidence: grep of session jsonl returned 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' (3+ hits); screen later shows 'Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans)' only after spec approval.

criteria.criterion: Classified as ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/*/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Assistant text in log: "That's new structure, so this moves from **bounded** to **architectural**. The ratchet is one-way: I'll run the full process — questions, approaches, a sectioned design, then a written spec — before any code." File exists: ./docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-design.md (head shows '# User Identity Design ... Status: Approved for planning').

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: 'Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-design.md (not committed)... Please review it and let me know if you want any changes before I write the implementation plan.' `git status --short` at that moment showed only '?? .gitignore' — no edits to app.js/index.html.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec
criteria.evidence: An initial line said 'This is a **bounded** change... So I'll settle the design in chat rather than write a spec', but it self-corrected to architectural and a spec file was committed to disk before approval (docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-user-identity-design.md).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / present a throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: jq over assistant text messages grepping 'spike' returned no matches; flow was questions → sectioned design → spec doc → plan.
